evidence.quote: Please be advised that the Township of Middle DOES NOT issue a Certificate of Occupancy or a Zoning Certificate for the transfer of a property/business nor for the renting of a property. The only time a Certificate of Occupancy is issued is at the origination of the building, change of use, reconstruction or an addition per the Uniform Construction Code 5:23-2.24.
10 South Boyd Street Cape May Court House, NJ 08210 Phone: (609) 465-8740

resale_co.notes: The Construction page says in writing that the Township does not issue a Certificate of Occupancy or a Zoning Certificate for the transfer of a property or for renting. The Construction Official's email comes from the mailto link on his name. Zoning Office: Rachel Shepherd, Zoning Officer, (609) 465-8742, rmshepherd@middletownship.com. The only resale item found is the fire district Bureau of Fire Prevention certificate (see fire_cert).

requirements: Smoke alarms by year built: before 1977, 10-year sealed battery alarms on each level and outside each sleeping area; newer homes need AC-powered (hardwired) alarms per the construction code of their year, interconnected from August 1984, and in each bedroom with battery backup from March 1991
Do not replace AC-powered alarms with battery alarms; alarms over 10 years old (or with no date) must be replaced; no tape or velcro mounting

Low-voltage fire alarm systems in homes built 1977 or later must be kept and tested by a NJ licensed alarm contractor, with the passed report sent to the Bureau before the inspection; systems installed 2011 or later must be monitored

CO alarm (UL 2034) in the hallway within 10 feet of each sleeping area when there is a fuel-burning appliance or attached garage, plus one in any bedroom with a fuel-burning appliance; not more than 10 years old

Portable fire extinguisher 2-A:10-B:C, no larger than 10 lbs, new or tagged within 12 months, on the manufacturer's bracket within 10 feet of the kitchen, top no higher than 5 feet (still listed in the 2025 packet)
Secondary power source label within 18 inches of the main electrical panel and meter for homes with solar, backup generators or batteries
Certificate will not be issued if there are any open construction permits

authorities.how_to_apply: Download the 2025 Home Sale Application Packet (CSACMAPFEC) from the Fire District 1 Forms page, complete and initial all 4 pages (seller must sign), and submit it with a check or money order payable to Bureau of Fire Prevention to 115 Mechanic Street, Cape May Court House, NJ 08210 (firebureau@cmchfire.com, 609-465-8710). Forms dated before August 2025 are not accepted. Applications left in the mailbox count as received the next business day. Office hours Monday to Thursday 8:00am to 4:00pm, Friday 8:00am to 1:00pm.

fire_cert.notes: The DCA registry lists four Middle Township fire districts (D) and notes that Fire District #1 is the local enforcing agency for Districts 2, 3 and 4, so one Bureau of Fire Prevention at 115 Mechanic Street handles smoke/CO certificates township-wide. The packet header still names Districts #1, 3 & 4 because District #2 had its own bureau office until April 27, 2026. The Fire Official's name comes from the state fire directory (Douglas Greenberg, greenbergdm@cmchfire.com); the Fire District 1 website names Keith P. Arenberg (609-780-3233, arenbergkp@cmchfire.com) as its general contact without a title. The 2025 packet still requires a portable fire extinguisher even though P.L.2025, c.19 removed it from the state requirement. A $500 penalty applies for transferring the property before the certificate is issued.
